post.description: Starts a Sign in with Google with an intent (sign_in or sign_up) and an optional same-origin returnTo path. It runs the OpenID Connect authorization-code flow with PKCE (S256), a state and a nonce, keeps them in an attempt that lives 10 minutes, sets a short-lived attempt cookie (named tula_oidc, with the __Secure- prefix outside local only, because Safari refuses a __Secure- cookie over http even on loopback) that holds the attempt secret, and answers the authorizationUrl to send the browser to (https, or http to a loopback host in local development; a consumer also checks its host against an allow-list). It asks for openid, email and profile only, with no offline access. The returnTo is checked against the portal route allow-list and kept in the attempt; it is never read from the callback. oidc.disabled (404) when Google is not set up; oidc.provider_unavailable (503) with a Retry-After header when Google cannot be reached.

get.summary: Sign in with Google: the redirect back
get.description: Where Google sends the browser back, with a code and a state (or an error). The state must match the attempt cookie and the attempt is single-use; a replayed, expired or mismatched state is oidc.state_invalid. If the person cancels at Google (error=access_denied) the code is oidc.access_denied, and any other error from Google is oidc.provider_unavailable. The code is exchanged once, with the PKCE verifier, and the ID token is verified (RS256 only, issuer, audience, expiry, nonce, a present sub and email, and a verified email). A Google account that is already known, by its sub and never by its email, is signed in with the same checks as a password sign-in, and the answer is a 302 to the portal with the refresh cookie on it. No token appears in a URL. A new Google user is created by nothing here: the 302 goes to /sign-up/google?attempt=<id> and the person finishes with complete. An existing password account with the same email is linked only when Google verified the email, else oidc.email_unverified. It answers every outcome with a 302 except oidc.disabled (404): a failure redirects the browser to /sign-in?error=<code>, so oidc.state_invalid, oidc.email_unverified, oidc.access_denied, oidc.provider_unavailable (whose catalogue status is 503, with a Retry-After header only where it is a real response), auth.user_banned, auth.no_organization, organization.deleted and membership.unavailable come back as the error parameter of that redirect, and the catalogue status of a code is not the HTTP status of this response. Codes, tokens and Authorization headers are never logged.

post.summary: Finish Sign in with Google for a new user
post.description: Finishes the sign-up of a new Google user: it takes the attempt id (the secret is in the cookie) and exactly one of an organizationName or an invitationToken. It creates the Organization or joins the invited one through the same sign-up path as an email sign-up, with no emailed code because Google verified the email, and stores the user and a google identity with no password. For an invitation the Google email must equal the invited address, else oidc.invitation_mismatch (403); a user who already belongs to an Organization gets membership.already_member (409). An attempt that is missing, used or expired is oidc.state_invalid (400). An attempt is single-use. A repeat is refused with oidc.state_invalid (400) and nothing is created twice. Answers the browser flow response (id, kind, expiresAt, a complete step and the session); the refresh token is in the cookie, never in the body. The attempt secret, tokens and the email are never logged.

post.description: Trades a refresh token for new tokens. Each refresh token works once; presenting a spent one after a short grace period ends the whole session (`session.reuse_detected`). If the core service cannot answer, the answer is 503 `membership.unavailable` with `Retry-After` and the refresh token is not spent: send the same one again. A user whose Organization was deleted gets `organization.deleted` and the session ends. Client type `browser` (`x-tula-client: browser`) sends no body: the refresh token is read from the cookie only (a body or header token is ignored, a missing cookie is `session.invalid_token`), `Origin` is checked first (`auth.forbidden`), and the new refresh token is set in the cookie and omitted from the body.
